A copy's ending (" (Copy)", " (Copy) (Copy)", " (conflict copy)") always shows. Three or more of one ending in a row show as one with a count (" (Copy ×6)"). A name that fits in two lines is one run of text, with the ending right after the last word. A longer name clamps only its base, and the ending stands beside the base's last line. The card measures this before paint, and again when the name or its width changes. Third review (71f5a7a): the reviewer's blocking finding is real. On 1d693cb the measurement was compared with the width the ResizeObserver last saw. That observer is off while Rename is open and while the name has no ending. So if the card was resized or rotated in those moments and the name then changed, every measurement looked stale and was redone before paint, until React threw "Maximum update depth exceeded" and the dashboard went blank. Now each measurement also records the width it was taken at, so the card measures once. The hover title and the stored name still hold the full text, and the two-column lg grid from 8a17031 is unchanged. | There is still no real-browser layout check at 1024 px. tests/pdf/104 uses a crude fake line layout (every `cpl` characters is one line), not real text metrics. A browser that reports scrollHeight one pixel over clientHeight for a name that fits would show the split layout, which is still correct but has a small gap. The name is not measured again when only the web fonts finish loading at the same width. The editor at /resume/B keeps showing and editing B the whole time; before, it showed and edited the imported résumé under B's address. There are two parts. (1) importResume (src/hooks/useResumeStore.js) no longer makes the imported résumé the open one. Every import that should open it navigates to /resume/:id, and useOpenResume opens it from there. An import made from the editor opens the imported résumé once; the old one no longer flashes back in between. Tests in 52-editor-route: (a) a stand-in store whose activeId moves while the address stays /resume/resume_b; (b) with the app's real store, an import plus navigation from the editor shows the imported résumé without A coming back, and a late import never shows in B's editor; (c) an import into an empty list is the open one. |  |
| R5-HUNT1-WORD-LIST-INDENT-360-VS-720 | r5-hunt1-export | ✅ Fixed | `bcbd2156da87be0c8a628769b9d682558756bdfe` | tests/pdf/105-r5-hunt1-word-list-indent.test.mjs | Now: in the Word export (résumé descriptions, the summary and the cover-letter body), numbered list items use the same geometry at every level as bullets. An item at level n has its text at 720 × (n + 1) twips, and its marker hangs 360 in front of it. That is how docx's default bullets (checked in docx 9.7.1: 720/1440/2160…, hanging 360) and bulletNumbering place theirs. A numbered list nested in a bullet now prints its '1.' at 1080, past the bullet's text at 720, and its text at 1440. Before, the '1.' sat in the bullet's glyph column and the text sat flush with the bullet's text. A top-level numbered list now lines up with top-level bullets (left 720). A further paragraph inside a list item starts at that item's text instead of under its glyph. A quote or <dd> outside any list lines up with a top-level item's text, as richText.js documents. The fix is in src/utils/wordExportUtils.js: LEVEL_TWIPS goes from 360 to 720, and a new MARKER_TWIPS = 360 sets the hanging indent. The Word importer reads list depth from w:ilvl or the list style, not from w:ind, so importing an exported file behaves as before. Stored data is not touched. |  |

| R5-HUNT1-ONE-PAGE-FIT-LOOSENS-TIGHT-SPACING-AND-SHRINKS-TEXT | r5-hunt1-pdf | ✅ Fixed | `f40a7fcfc4beb20f592f047363206f49ff4c40b4` | tests/pdf/r5hunt1-fit-keeps-tight-spacing.test.mjs | Now: every 1-Page Fit step takes, for marginV, marginH, sectionGap, itemGap and lineHeightValue, the smaller of the step's own value and the value the résumé has stored (fitLadder in src/utils/pageFit.js). This includes the preset that is written at once: DesignPanel now takes it from fitLadder(settings)[0] instead of ONE_PAGE_FIT. A step that comes out the same as the one before it is dropped. Before, the preset (10/14 mm, gaps 10/5 px, line height 1.35) was written over whatever the résumé had, and the tightest step stopped at 5/8 mm, 4/2 px and 1.2, while the panel goes down to 0 mm, 0 px and 1.0. A résumé that fitted on one page at hand-tuned tighter spacing was loosened onto a second page, and the ladder then brought the text down ('Fits on 1 page — text size 11 → 10 pt'). Now such a résumé keeps its spacing and its text size, and no notice is shown. The text size comes down only when the user's own spacing, tightened as far as the ladder goes, still runs past one page. A résumé that is tighter on only some keys keeps those keys and still takes the ladder's values for the others. Unset keys print at the renderer's defaults (1.5, 14/18 mm, 16/8 px), which are all looser than the preset, so their behaviour is unchanged. Stored values are already numbers clamped to the panel's ranges (withSpacingNumbers at load), so old data cannot put a non-number or an out-of-range value into a step. Not done (by design): an 'already fits, change nothing' check before the preset, because R2-149 writes the preset at once and 91-page-fit, 86-line-height-shown, 69-word-spacing, Cypress 30-starters-and-design and the Playwright pdf-typography-spacing spec rely on that. Also not done: Undo for 1-Page Fit. |  |
| R5-HUNT1-RESUME-SYNC-OTHER-TAB-SIGNOUT-DELETES-ALL | r5-hunt1-sync | ✅ Fixed | `2a354d3b084ef74b774eb1ae30de9366891bdc9c`, `56c71592efc6a06e2ab58c9cd4f6f4e00d6e5b89` | tests/pdf/18-cloud-sync-sign-out.test.mjs | Now: when another tab takes this tab's résumé list away before this tab's own Firebase Auth has noticed, this tab sends nothing. That happens when the other tab signs out (cloudSyncLeave.js empties the list and sets syncedUid null) or signs in as another account (the list becomes that account's). A hidden tab's auth poll is throttled, so the gap can be long. resumesChanged (src/utils/cloudSyncQueue.js) now checks whether the store's syncedUid is still the signed-in uid. If it is not, it drops its queue, sets initialSyncDone = false and returns. The sync starts again at the next first sync, which runs when this tab's auth reports the sign-out or the new account. Before this fix, the list that arrived was compared with the account's list. An empty list was sent as hard-deletes plus deletion-list entries for every résumé, so every device dropped its copies too. Another account's list was written into this account's cloud. The guard is the same one collectionSyncEngine.js already had for jobs and boards (meta uid !== s.user.uid). The store's syncedUid always equals the uid once a first sync has applied (afterSync). Only cloudSyncLeave sets it to anything else, and every store updater spreads prev. So an ordinary same-account session never hits the guard. useCloudSync updates its latest-state ref in an effect declared before the resumesChanged effect, so the guard reads the same render's state. | While this tab's auth has not caught up, its sync icon keeps its last status ('synced', or 'syncing' if a flush was pending) until start() runs. This is cosmetic, and the jobs and boards sync behaves the same way. |

| R5-HUNT3-JOB-STORE-STALE-WRITE-AFTER-LEAVING-JOB-PAGES | r5-hunt3-jobs | ✅ Fixed | `d0ab6e3ec36a6fb41b08454a449e4cbe9af5bc8b`, `4c250801601774960192ff8497a1f6b0bd1ca07d`, `6488d67c5c0c71521f705b23f309504a0cb23b81` | tests/unit/job-store-detached.unit.mjs | Now: while no job page is open, the job store stops listening to other tabs (J-01). Before it reads or writes its list, snapshot() now calls catchUp(). catchUp() compares the raw stored value with what this tab last saw (seenRaw). Only when that value has changed does it read the list again with the pure readStored/peek and keep what storage refused in this tab (keepUnsaved). Because it runs only on a change, the snapshot stays the same object while storage is unchanged, and a render still writes nothing (NB-6). As a result, an Undo on a deleted job, on 'N jobs cleared' or on a deleted task, clicked after leaving the job pages, puts back only what was deleted and keeps the other tab's jobs and edits. A job form reopened later first renders the job as it is stored now, not this tab's old copy. Review fix 4c25080: the re-read made no backup, so an Undo or edit wrote over a value that could not be read in full and lost it. That value can come from another tab of a newer build saving a status this one does not know. Now setJobs copies it first (backupRaw), as load() does. Signed in with the cloud on, the sync keeps a subscription open, so the old path (storage event) still applies there. The change is in src/hooks/useJobStore.js only, and the knowledge docs (05) are updated. |  |

| R5-HUNT4-RECOVERY-BACKUP-SURVIVES-SIGNOUT | r5-hunt4-sync | ✅ Fixed | `381cc6addcbe26940f220cb4d04fb53058b11bea`, `772c3b3fff321b8d79450b5a17ebd33a06707342` | tests/unit/recovery-leaves-with-account.unit.mjs, tests/pdf/106-r5-hunt4-resume-recovery-leaves-with-account.test.mjs | Now: when an account's résumés, jobs or boards leave this browser (it signs out, or another account signs in while the list is still the last one's: R2-005), the list's recovery notice (<key>_recovery, including a notice held in memory because storage was full) and every raw backup of it (<key>_backup_<ms>) leave too. The notice is also taken off the open page. The next person can no longer download the previous account's list from the Dashboard, the Job Tracker or the board pages. How: a new storageBackup.forgetRecovery(key), and leaveRecovery() in useAppStore, useJobStore and boardStoreState. For jobs and boards, collectionSyncEngine.leave calls store.leaveRecovery?.() only after leaveList has confirmed the list is that account's (meta.uid === uid); jobSync and boardSync pass the stores' functions. For résumés, liveStore.leaveAccount calls store.leaveRecovery?.() only when appState.syncedUid === uid, the same condition cloudSyncLeave.leaveAccount uses. A list no account ever synced, or one in a build with no cloud, keeps its notice and backups, because it is still this browser's. Trade-off: entries of the account's own list that could not be read, and were never in its cloud, are deleted on sign-out rather than kept aside for its next sign-in. The finding named deleting as acceptable. Review: the tests now load without the fix and fail at their assertions. Two added cases drive the real useAppStore through liveStore. | (1) A second tab that already shows the notice keeps showing it until reload, but its Download finds nothing because the backup is gone. Nothing leaks. (2) A résumé store whose whole value is unparseable JSON loads with syncedUid null. If the owner's session ended before that load, nobody's leave matches the list, and its backup and notice stay for the next account. This needs a corrupt store and an expired session together, and the owner cannot be read from an unreadable value. (3) Notices and backups left behind by builds before this fix cannot be attributed to an account, so they are not cleaned up. |

| R5-HUNT5-PASTE-WORD-BULLETS-BECOME-MIDDOT-PARAGRAPHS | r5-hunt5-editor | ✅ Fixed | `c08852d89d6223ea0bb55295b6f0806b874b1c28`, `bd23db66014a6bd0085470072c224965a6dfb139` | tests/unit/r5-hunt5-paste-word-bullets.unit.mjs, tests/unit/r5-hunt5-paste-word-lists-review.unit.mjs | Now: a list pasted from Word for desktop becomes a real <ul> or <ol>. A numbered marker such as '1.' or 'a)' makes an <ol>. A new list starts when the kind changes, or when the list id changes at level 1. All of this is in parseRichText (src/utils/richText.js): buildTree keeps the marker in its own #mso-marker node, marked closed at <![endif]>; wordLists() groups p/div/h* items; the walk skips only closed markers. A failed takedown is retried at the next first sync.
